title: Fable + Three.js + 3D AI Is a Wildly Useful Game Dev Workflow
author: Delicious-Shower8401
selftext:
I’ve been working on my own **dice-based roguelike** for the last few days, and right now I’m mostly focused on the part that matters most early on: the overall feel.

I’m trying to get the core loop right, improve the micro-interactions, shape the atmosphere, and make the whole thing feel more alive. It’s a small indie project, and I’m building it mostly on my own, so I’m constantly looking for workflows that actually help instead of just looking impressive on paper.

And honestly, this setup feels kind of crazy already. I’m pretty sure I’m using maybe **1% of what this whole AI workflow can really do**, but even now it’s saving me a lot of time.

Current setup looks like this:

* **UI is built in Three.js**, with no HTML/CSS
* **The three charms** were generated in **3DAIStudio using Tripo P2**
* **The table** was modeled manually by me
* **The dice are procedurally generated**
* **PBR/material work** was done through **3DAIStudio**
* **The UI and structure** were designed first, then I used **Fable** to help implement the system

I also want to test how far I can push this next. I’m curious what this clanker can do overnight if I give it a task like:

>“Reuse my current UI component system for the rest of the game and rework everything, including the micro-interactions.”

Not expecting magic, but this kind of workflow genuinely saves time.

Also, quick credit where it’s due: **3DAIStudio** has been really useful because the **node-based workflow** makes everything feel much more organized and flexible. And **Tripo P2** deserves praise too — the models coming out of it are genuinely solid and often don’t need much manual cleanup, which makes the whole process much faster.
